subject: if-st-dy
title: IF.ST.DY.------C.CONT.
description: Diagram in PCC-22, the section where Braxton outlines the La Monte Young / Terry Riley / Reich / Glass continuum as 'the first aesthetic, after the destruction of the classical vibrational hierarchy, to utilize and reintegrate spiritualism as a real part of the meta-reality of its process.' (C)IF-ST-DY (infra-structure dynamics) is crossed with C-CONT (composite continuance): the question is what infrastructure dynamics looks like when crossed with composite continuance in the minimalist/spiritualist context, where Young/Riley's drone-based work was structurally distinct from Cage's existential exercise. (R)MTH (the reality of methodology) → IF-ST-DY; IST-F (isolated focus) → MT-DEVF (multiple diversification) → IF-ST-DY. IF-ST-DY → C-CONT (the crossing) → STF (source transfer). A separate chain: LANG-DY (language dynamics) → SOC-RT-DY (social reality dynamics) → CULT-AF-BS (culture affinity basis) → POST (postulation), with INFO-OR (information order) also → CULT-AF-BS. Structural argument: infrastructure dynamics is fed by both real methodology and isolated-focus-via-multiple-diversification — meaning Young/Riley's contribution required *both* a real methodological grounding (not merely conceptual) *and* the isolated-focus-multiple-diversification path that western pedagogy had failed to provide. Composite continuance produces source transfer as its terminal output, while the parallel postulation chain runs language → social-reality → culture-affinity-basis (with information-order as co-feed) → postulation. The diagram thus stages the structural conditions under which the minimalist movement's source-transfer with eastern forms (Young's drones, Riley's repetition) actually produced composite continuance rather than merely fashionable adoption.
